title: MMDFL: Multi-Model-based Decentralized Federated Learning for Resource-Constrained AIoT Systems
problem: Decentralized federated learning on resource-constrained AIoT devices faces challenges from limited computing/bandwidth, non-IID data, and expensive all-neighbor aggregation.
motivation: Centralized FL suffers single-point-of-failure and communication bottlenecks; DFL avoids parameter server but still struggles with resource constraints.
method: MMDFL works by sending multiple model copies between devices, where each device trains its models on its own local data. The system intelligently picks which devices to collaborate with based on how different their data is from others and how much computing power each device has. Instead of requiring every device to share knowledge with all its neighbors (a dense, expensive communication pattern), the knowledge-sharing step works independently from these neighbor connections, which cuts down total communication overhead.
key_novelty: Using multiple traveling models that adaptively choose which devices to connect with based on data diversity and available resources, rather than requiring communication with all neighbors.
contributions: Multi-model-based learning framework using traveler models for distributed knowledge sharing
Adaptive device selection strategy accounting for data heterogeneity, resource constraints, and catastrophic forgetting
Significant reduction in communication overhead vs state-of-the-art DFL methods
Improved classification performance for both IID and non-IID data scenarios

metrics.other: reduced communication overhead, improved accuracy on IID/non-IID data

limitations: Scalability limits and overhead for very large-scale deployments not thoroughly discussed.
primary_theme: Decentralized federated learning for resource-constrained IoT devices
